newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks finish sleepy session slighly firmer.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks finish sleepy session slighly firmer.

text.p: Australian shares edged to a slightly higher close on Monday with light buying interest in the bank sector supporting the market as it wound down for the Christmas break.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed 6.7 points higher at 2,380.5, not far from its intra-day high of 2,384.7.
Turnover was about a third of the market's record one session volume of A$1.7 billion, which was set on Friday.
"It was the sort of trade you expect for this time of year - fairly lumpy. I certainly wouldn't want to read to much into it," a dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage said.

The dealer said the two factors supporting the market on the day were some selective bargain hunting and interest in the bank sector following the Advance Bank shareholder's approval of a scheme to merge with fellow regional St George Bank.
"The approval appears to clinch the deal for St George and although this was bad for its shares, it was good for Advance and National Australia Bank stock," the dealer said.
St George stock ended 19 cents weaker at A$7.88 (US$6.30) while Advance shares advanced 16 cents to A$6.90 and National Australia Bank stock rose 14 cents to A$14.63.
